source_facts:
- Professor Kim's cell-biology lecture is on Tuesday.
- Optional microscopy workshop is on Friday in Room 214.
- Mitochondria produce ATP, the usable energy for cellular processes.
- Ribosomes assemble proteins by translating messenger RNA.
- Plant cells have cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts.
- Animal cells lack cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts.
- Mature human red blood cells lack nuclei to allow more space for hemoglobin.
- Robert Hooke published observations of cork cells in 1665.
- Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy.
- Active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient and requires energy.
- The sodium-potassium pump is an example of active transport.
- Chapter 7 is assigned for Monday.
- Professor Kim's Wednesday office hours moved from 2:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. due to a faculty meeting.

source_facts:
- The North Campus laboratory handbook covers the wet lab, machine shop, greenhouse, and instrument room.
- Trained researchers enter the wet lab by scanning an active badge.
- Visitors without safety training may enter only when escorted by a certified technician who must stay with them until they leave.
- Food and drinks are prohibited in all experimental rooms.
- Food and drinks may be stored in the second-floor lounge.
- Chemical deliveries arrive at loading dock C.
- Chemical deliveries must be logged by a staff member before storage.
- Reference samples normally cannot leave the building.
- A principal investigator may authorize an overnight loan of reference samples by signing form RS-4.
- After three failed badge scans, access is disabled for twenty minutes.
- Spills larger than 500 milliliters require evacuation and a call to campus emergency services.
- Smaller spills may be handled by trained staff using the appropriate spill kit.
- Eyewash stations are tested every Monday.
- Incident reports must be submitted within 24 hours.
- The handbook undergoes an annual review in March.
- Outdated printed copies of the handbook should be placed in secure recycling, not ordinary bins.

source_facts:
- Saturday's research conference registration starts at 8:00 a.m. in the student center.
- Data-visualization tutorial begins at 9:00 a.m. in Room 32-123.
- Hardware-prototyping tutorial starts at 9:00 a.m. in Maker Studio B.
- Machine-learning keynote begins at 10:30 a.m. in Kresge Auditorium; doors open at 10:15 a.m.
- Lunch is served at noon in Walker Memorial; vegetarian meals are marked by green cards.
- Poster session runs from 1:15 to 2:45 p.m. in Johnson Track, featuring 84 posters.
- Robotics demonstration moved from Building 26 to the Stata Center and delayed until 3:20 p.m. due to equipment issues.
- Shuttle buses to the evening reception depart from Massachusetts Avenue every 20 minutes starting at 5:40 p.m.
- Evening reception starts at 6:00 p.m. in the MIT Museum.
- Attendees who lose a badge should visit the welcome desk.
- Lost physical items are held at campus police until Monday.
- Best-poster award, a $500 equipment grant, will be announced during the reception at 7:15 p.m.
